big: A resident of India is taxed on income from anywhere in the world. An NRI is taxed in India only on income earned or received in India. Meena earns a salary in Singapore and rent in Pune. Only the rent counts.

lines: Is my Singapore salary taxable in India?
Not while you are a non-resident. India taxes your Indian income. Interest on an NRE account is generally exempt in India. Payers deduct tax at source on Indian income, often at higher rates.

rows: Not taxed in India while she is an NRI
note: Rules change, so check the current rule with your bank or a qualified adviser.

title: What India taxes
stops: Residents are taxed on world income in India
NRIs are taxed on income earned abroad in India
NRO interest is taxable in India
NRE interest is generally taxed in India
caps: Global income is taxed for residents.
NRIs are taxed on Indian-sourced income.
It arises in India, so India taxes it.
NRE interest is generally exempt while non-resident.

q: Meena earns a salary in Singapore as an NRI. Does India tax it?
opts: Yes, in full, as he is Indian
Yes, but only half of the salary
Only on festival days of the year
why: A salary earned abroad is generally not taxed here.
There is no half-and-half rule for a foreign salary.
India taxes NRIs on income sourced in India.
Festival days have no link to tax on salary.

q: Rohan receives rent in his NRO account. What follows?
opts: It is exempt, as she lives abroad
It is taxed only in outer space
It is treated as a gift to her
why: Rent from Indian property is Indian-source income.
It is not exempt, since it arises in India.
No tax of that kind exists anywhere in the law.
Rent is income and is not treated as a gift.

q: What is generally true of interest on an NRE account?
opts: Taxed at a very high rate there
Never paid on such an account
Paid in gold bars at maturity
why: It is not taxed at a very high rate in India.
Interest is paid on such accounts every year.
It is paid in rupees and not in gold bars.
NRE interest is generally exempt while the holder is an NRI.

q: A buyer deducts tax at a higher rate on a payment to an NRI. What is this?
opts: A fee charged by the bank
A gift sent by the buyer
why: A bank's fee is a charge by the bank and not by the buyer.
Tax is deducted at source, often at higher rates for NRIs.
It is not a gift, since it goes to the tax office.
It is not an insurance charge of any kind.

pts: Residents are taxed on world income. NRIs on Indian-source income.
NRO interest is taxable. NRE interest is generally exempt.
Payers deduct TDS on NRI income, often at higher rates.
